newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended Friday trade weaker after it was knocked by a large import order in the morning and failed to recover during the day.
Forex traders expected a weaker bias at the start of next week with a forecast range of between 4.5850 and 4.6150.
The local unit ended the day at 4.6005/6055 on the dollar after an intraday high bid of 4.6060 and from 4.5740/5790 at the Thursday finish.
"The (local) guys were looking for dollars when the market was already short this morning and we then saw some dollar inflows from offshore around the 4.6050 level," a senior forex trader said.
However, these were countered by more foreign and local dollar demand during the afternoon session.
Traders said sentiment was nervous and several believed the immediate bias was towards the topside.
"Sentiment is turning weaker again," one commented after the rand put in a strong performance earlier in the week following last week's one percentage point hike in interest rates.
Other forex traders said this week they expected the rand to hold broadly steady going into December, in a wide 4.52 to 4.62 band.
The rand was last trading at 7.7317/7447 on sterling from 7.6924/7054 on Thursday. It was little changed at 0.3332/3337 marks from 0.3345/3350 previously.
Long bond yields ended below the 15.90 percent level after what one dealer described as "a confusing week".

"All technical traders and analysts were very positive earlier this week when yields broke through the key 15.80 percent chart level which was regarded as a bullish break and now we are all the way back near 15.90 percent again," a bond trader said.

At 1405 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was at 15.88 percent from 15.81 percent late on Thursday as the market awaited the release of Ocober money supply and private sector credit extension figures at 1500 GMT.
Traders said there was concern about fundamentals, including the continued high money market shortage and expectations that the private sector credit and money supply data would be poor.
The consensus forecast of 13 economists polled by Reuters was that private sector credit extension expanded 18.1 percent year-on-year in October, with the forecast range 17.7 to 18.6.
This compares with a preliminary September figure of 17.94 percent, but this is expected to be revised upwards when the latest data is released.
M3 money supply growth is forecast at 15.1 percent -- with a range 14.1 to 15.5 percent -- after September's 14.45 percent.

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.00 percent and 17.10 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 16.40 and 16.65 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.377 billion rand on Thursday from 9.071 billion rand on Wednesday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 111.64 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying a net 244.28 million rand worth of bonds on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 37.44 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 9.81 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
